title: Start a new procedure light
statement: Make the first lesson on a new procedure lighter, with a smaller set to work on, built so later lessons only widen the set instead of rebuilding it.
example: The first lesson on one procedure showed students three sentences to choose from; the second had them pick from the whole section.
detail: Two persuasive-text lesson designs plan a fade across a unit. The first deliberately lightens its find-the-opinions task to a reduced set of three sentences, written so that lightening later only means widening that set, and the second applies the fade: the child taps opinions straight from the whole section. Both are design notes logged for confirmation.
against: The first comparison lesson went the other way: "Built here to the KB row as-is: the full compare (similarities and differences, then connect)." It left lightening optional "(easier to fade than to build up)", though it too was written so that lightening only means trimming one step, not rebuilding the lesson.

The delivered approach is arguably cleaner for the unit's first FIND lesson, reducing the evidence set from 3 to 1 to limit cognitive load in the modelled walk-through.
